newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kobe Steel, others tie up for Chernobyl project.
newsitem.headline: Kobe Steel, others tie up for Chernobyl project.

text.p: Kobe Steel Ltd said on Tuesday it had formed a consortium with four European and U.S. firms to bid for a 200-billion-yen contract to scrap the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in the Ukraine.
The multinational consortium includes Britain's BNFL Engineering Ltd, Germany's Nukem Nuklear GmbH, France's Technicatome SA and Morrison Knudsen International Inc of the United States.
The specific schedule for the international tender has yet to be clear, a spokesman for the steel maker said.
Kobe Steel, which supplies power firms in Japan with steel containers for radioactive nuclear waste, would be in charge of processing and storage of nuclear waste from the site, he said.
The Chernobyl nuclear power station, whose number 4 reactor exploded in 1986 in the worst civilian nuclear accident in history, is due to be closed by 2000.

Last month, the seven major industrialised powers (G7) -- the United States, Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan -- promised Ukraine $300 million to help rebuild the concrete shell, or sarcophagus, hurriedly built around the number 4 unit following the accident.
